before:
\paragraph{Reproducibility limits.}
The polar implementation stores an integer weight table with row and column order HD, HA, HP and AR, denoting hydrogen-bond donor, hydrogen-bond acceptor, hydrophobe and aromatic features. It divides entries by 10000 to obtain dimensionless native weights. The v2 implementation multiplies its weight-table entries by 10000 and rounds before optimisation, then divides the clique sum by 10000. These weights are not binding energies. The complete custom weight tables are not included in the supplied manuscript, so their entries cannot be reconstructed from this account.
after:
\paragraph{Exact supporting records.}
The complete polar weight table is \texttt{audit.py}, \texttt{WEIGHTS}, with row/column \texttt{ORDER} HD, HA, HP, AR (donor, acceptor, hydrophobe, aromatic). Divide its integer entries by 10000 for dimensionless native scores. The corresponding v2 table is \texttt{v2\_wl.py}, \texttt{W}; \texttt{solve} multiplies entries by 10000 and rounds, then divides the clique sum by 10000. These weights are not binding energies.

before: The polar calculation reads PDB coordinates and aligns structures using a specified atom correspondence. after: All four fixed polar coordinates and atom identities are recorded in \texttt{polar-correction-results.json}, key \texttt{fixed\_receptor\_features}. before: The v2 calculation reads endpoint coordinate files and uses atom positions or arithmetic centroids of aromatic rings. Its receptor domain includes every eligible feature with a constituent atom at most 5~\AA\ from a ligand heavy atom. There is no nearest-four truncation or distance-ranking tie in that selection. No uniquely tie-broken optimum clique is claimed. The complete aromatic-ring construction procedure and the archive-source mapping for every predictive ligand are not supplied here. These omissions limit independent reproduction; the rules below do not establish physical calibration or the executable conventions of Ding and colleagues.
after: V2's \texttt{load}/\texttt{read\_crd} read each endpoint's SYSTEM.crd; the existing source table and \texttt{PRIMARY}/\texttt{ALT} identify archive edges and states. \texttt{features} uses atom positions or aromatic-ring arithmetic centroids. \texttt{receptor\_points} includes every eligible feature with a constituent atom at most 5~\AA\ from a ligand heavy atom: no nearest-four truncation or distance-ranking tie is involved. The same implementation specifies aromatic-ring construction; no unique tie-broken optimum witness is claimed. \texttt{solve} defines integer-weight clique scoring and the strict positive edge margin, excluding equality. For polar edges use \texttt{polar\_correction.py:corrected\_big}, not the preceding \texttt{audit.py} graph implementation. The model-specific allowances, reuse and preparation limits below remain; these records establish neither physical calibration nor the executable conventions of Ding and colleagues.
